findings.statement: CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed mucosa come almost entirely from neutrophils (neutrophil share [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]); Smillie, which lacks neutrophils, assigns it to T/NK cells and the second dataset to myeloid cells, so the attribution does not replicate. After composition adjustment the change shrinks to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409] (verdict partly_composition), so it mainly reports neutrophil influx; a drug would target neutrophils, not the tissue.

CXCR1 is a neutrophil-influx marker: [gene=CXCR1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.962] of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts are neutrophil-derived, so its high convergence rank mostly reflects cell arrival.

CXCL8 is made by myeloid cells (macrophages, inflammatory monocytes, DC2) in Smillie, replicated in the second dataset, but neutrophils contribute [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873] of inflamed transcripts. The bulk increase loses significance after composition adjustment [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523] (verdict composition); adjustment may over-correct if resident cells are activated, so this is not proof of pure influx.

MMP1 is a stromal product, with inflammatory fibroblasts the top cluster in inflamed mucosa [gene=MMP1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.531]; the attribution replicates in the second dataset and neutrophils contribute little. The change survives adjustment [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636] (verdict partly_composition, still significant), supporting a fibroblast-intrinsic tissue change.

In Visium, the fibroblast score co-varies most with MMP1 across spots [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium; source=DATASET:GSE189184; compartment_rho=0.191], ranking first in only two of three UC sections used; the correlation is weak and spot-level. MMP1 is not on the Xenium panel.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes and immature enterocytes), with an epithelial lineage share of [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947] replicated in the second dataset and confirmed in Xenium single cells and Visium; neutrophils contribute little. The bulk change is retained after adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] (partly_composition, still significant), a tissue-intrinsic epithelial response.

IDO1 is produced by myeloid cells (macrophages, DC1) in Smillie and the second dataset agrees; neutrophils make little of it, and the Gubatan data also shows enterocytes as the top state. The change persists after adjustment [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505] (partly_composition), so it is not mere neutrophil influx.

IL1B is myeloid-made but [gene=IL1B; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.702] of inflamed transcripts are neutrophil-derived, and the bulk change is not significant after adjustment [gene=IL1B; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0728] (verdict composition), so it behaves as a marker of myeloid and neutrophil influx; the adjustment may over-correct for activated resident cells.

AQP9 is overwhelmingly neutrophil-derived [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92], yet some change remains after adjustment [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551] (partly_composition); mainly an influx marker.

S100A8 transcripts are mostly neutrophil-derived [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909], with a residual significant change after adjustment [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231] (partly_composition); a neutrophil-activity biomarker rather than a tissue-cell target.

CHI3L1 has a mixed origin (neutrophils make under half of inflamed transcripts) and keeps a strong change after adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967] (partly_composition), so it reflects both a tissue change and influx.

TREM1 transcripts in inflamed mucosa are largely neutrophil-derived (about nine tenths in Gubatan 2026), so its bulk rise mainly signals neutrophil and myeloid influx; composition adjustment was not run for it.

caveats: Smillie 2019 has no neutrophils, so genes made by neutrophils are misattributed to other clusters (for example CXCR2 to T/NK); the Gubatan dataset corrects this.
Cell shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.

Composition adjustment can over-correct when resident cells become activated: genes losing significance (CXCL8, IL1B) are not proven pure influx, while genes keeping it (MMP1, DUOX2, IDO1, CHI3L1) are strong evidence of a tissue change.
Visium spots contain several cells and only a few UC sections ranked the lead lineage first; MMP1 is not on the Xenium panel.
Only a subset of the top-40 candidates was examined (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, IDO1, MMP1, DUOX2, IL1B, AQP9, S100A8, CHI3L1, TREM1); CD274, MMP3, CXCL1 were only checked for neutrophil share.
